title: approvals/messaging: the approval Slack DM and the approval email build their deep link from different origins — share one source so a host that sets only publicBaseUrl still gets an absolute DM link
body:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czKnDE6hsyXQzB9wB2

Filing gate: ② contract review N3 on PR #35789 (record 7037841566), the publicBaseUrl scope-out of #34730 step 2. ⛔ Not a claim.

**What.** After #35789, the approval email's deep link uses `ApprovalsServicePlugin`'s `publicBaseUrl` option first, while the Slack DM makes the link absolute from the deployment origin chain (`OS_AUTH_URL`, legacy `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, then `OS_BASE_URL`). A host that sets only `publicBaseUrl` gets an absolute link in the email and none in the DM. The two also normalise differently: the DM goes through `URL`, the email concatenates the raw value, so a mixed-case host or a default port gives the same destination in different bytes.

**Ask.** One origin source for both: e.g. the producer hands an absolute link in the notification payload that the slack channel prefers, or both read one shared resolver. Pin: a host with only `publicBaseUrl` set gets the same absolute destination in the email and the DM.

Blocked-by: #35789.
Suggested-grade: p3 · only hosts that set publicBaseUrl apart from their env origin.
Related: #34862 (the email link may miss the /_console mount; a different defect on the email side, but a shared resolver would carry both).
Dedupe: `publicBaseUrl` (2 hits: #34862, #34730), `deep link origin` (searched before filing).
